page: Amazon Web Services x2gd.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores on the 64-bit ARMv8 architecture, utilizing AWS Neoverse-N1 processors running at 2.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 512.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 1900 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 12 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate average multi-core capabilities, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 48,566.12 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 11,488.0. However, single-core performance is a relative bottleneck; the Geekbench single-core score of 942.0 and single-threaded gzip compression are categorized as weak, while single-threaded bzip3 decompression is poor at 7.26 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth is robust for cached operations, reaching 1894.65 GB/sec for small blocks, but drops to 139.81 GB/sec for uncached large block reads.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the x2gd.8xlarge offers high memory density and integrated NVMe storage on an ARM-based architecture, which typically yields lower operational costs compared to x86 equivalents with similar memory footprints. This profile is highly suitable for memory-intensive workloads, including relational databases, Redis caching layers, and medium-scale data processing. It is less suited for single-threaded compute tasks or heavy LLM text generation, where its performance is constrained.
